entities.summary:
Ya'ammu Nubwoserre was a ruler during the Second Intermediate Period of Egypt, traditionally placed in the Sixteenth Dynasty. As an Asiatic-blooded ruler, Nubwoserre holds significance in the historical context of ancient Egypt. His rule was part of the larger complex of political shifts during this era.

Nubwoserre Ya'ammu is notable for his involvement in the regional politics of ancient Egypt during the Second Intermediate Period. His reign was marked by the transition of power from the Hyksos to the Theban pharaohs, a period marked by significant cultural and political upheaval.

The legacy of Nubwoserre Ya'ammu can be seen in the eventual rise of the New Kingdom and the reunification of Egypt under the pharaohs of Thebes.

A lasting cultural footprint of Nubwoserre's reign can be found in the art and architecture of the period, which continues to inspire scholars and enthusiasts alike.
